T1_assumption_A_and_coupling_direction.statement_checked: log eps part of I^CT[eps] = hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/((X,Y) 16 pi^2) log eps (Q + {I,-})(2 int(A,A^*) - 4 int(lambda^*,lambda) - int(c^*,c)) in every sector with superficial degree >= 0; coefficient along the coupling direction = 0.
why_it_survives: The bracket with 2int(A,A^*) - 4int(lambda^*,lambda) - int(c^*,c) is the field count with weights A:2, lambda:4, c:1 and antifields with the opposite weights (rederived with the [C07] Delta_0 and the manuscript K_0; the signs -4 and -1 come from lambda^*, c^* being the even members of their pairs). Applied to S it gives the multiples 4 (quadratic gauge), 8 (lambda kinetic), -1 ((dc,A^*)), 6, 10, 1, 1, 1 (cubic), 8 (quartic): all eleven cubic/quartic sets agree.
Uniqueness: beta S + {S, general weight functional} with beta and four weights is overdetermined by 15 sector equations; the gauge multiples (2,3,4) x weight + beta (1,1,1) force beta = 0, weight 2.

Completeness at one loop: by power counting (A:1, lambda:3/2, c:0, A^*:3, lambda^*:5/2, c^*:4, ghost number 0, density dimension <= 4) the only local structures are those already in S (no A^*A^*, lambda^*lambda^* or c^* A terms); Spin(6)-odd and eps^{-1/2} pieces are excluded by invariance. Hence (A) is not only 'verified to the extent computed' but holds at one loop given the computed sets.

General simple g: engine B reduces ordered adjoint traces exactly (symmetrised quartic trace kept separately); its symmetrised-trace coefficient totals vanish in all three quartic sets, so the quartic statement does not rest on su(2) identities. Engine A alone is su(2).

caveats.text: Coupling direction representative: d/ds S[(1+s)(-,-)] = S also rescales the BV pairing (antifields are identified through (-,-)), so it is not a deformation inside the fixed BV complex. Inside the fixed complex the coupling direction is the classical part of S (the terms without antifields); the difference, the antifield terms of S, equals (Q + {I,-})(-int(c^*,c)) (ghost-number count). Because the fit contains the c-weight, beta is unchanged and the conclusion stands; the text should say this.

The most general degree -1 weight-4 functional has two independent lambda terms (the two four-dimensional chiralities of lambda^*, lambda). The fits use one weight; equality of the two weights is forced by the chirality-odd structure in the (lambda,lambda,A|_Wperp) set (multiple of tree 10 in both structures). State it.

The quartic statement for general simple g rests on engine B only (engine A is su(2), where every invariant of four adjoints is a combination of products of (-,-)); the third independent check covers bosonic classes only.

T2_QME_defect.verdict: CONFIRMED for the quadratic sector (numbers independently reproduced); scope of the conclusion must be restricted

details: D = Q J + 1/2 {J,J}_eps + hbar Delta_eps J with J = I - I^CT[eps]; Q W(P(eps,infty),J) = sum of connected graphs with one D vertex (UV-boundary identity).

Order hbar^0: QI + 1/2{I,I}_eps = 1/2({I,I}_eps - {I,I}_0) by the CME; the special edge is K_eps - K_0 (field-antifield components only). Equivalent to [C07] (12.0.1) (special edge K_eps plus the vertex QI, since 1/2{I_3,I_3}_0 = -Q I_4).

Order hbar: Delta_eps I - Q I^CT[eps] - {I, I^CT[eps]}_eps (signs from QJ and from 1/2{J,J}_eps); Delta_eps I = 0 because every antifield vertex is ([X,c],Y)-type and the contraction with the inverse pairing gives ([t,c],t)-sums = 0.

Factor 1/2: the bubble with special edge and one P(eps,infty) line has weight 1 after the 1/2 of 1/2{I,I} and the two orderings; route (b) (Q applied to the plain self-energy) reproduces route (a) exactly, which fixes the factor and sign of the special-edge implementation.

Which terms enter for external (c, A|_V): only the special-edge bubbles (one-loop two-point graphs with one special edge are bubbles; tadpole-type graphs vanish by colour) and -Q I^CT[eps]; {I, I^CT}_eps is cubic. Census complete.

caveats.text: The cancellation of eps^{-1} and the absence of log eps in the quadratic sector are automatic: Q is linear and preserves polynomial degree, so the quadratic part of Q W(P(eps,infty), I - I^CT[eps]) equals Q of (quadratic part of W_1 minus quadratic part of I^CT[eps]), and the latter is finite by the very construction of I^CT[eps] as the singular part of the same two-point function. The check validates the special-edge implementation of the UV-boundary identity, not the quantum master equation.
caveats.fix: Present the quadratic result as: finite obstruction = Q of the finite longitudinal part of the renormalised A|_V two-point function, (27/16) hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/((X,Y) 16 pi^2) int(d^*A|_V, d^*A|_V).

caveats.text: Q-exactness in this sector is automatic: the only ghost-number-1, dimension-4, Spin(4) x Spin(6) x Ad-invariant quadratic local functional is int(d^*dc, d^*A|_V) = -1/2 Q int(d^*A|_V, d^*A|_V) (int(dc, d^*dA|_V) = 0). The cohomologically meaningful statement is (Q + {I,-})-exactness of the full one-loop obstruction, which needs the cubic sector (OPEN). Adding the finite counterterm changes the cubic obstruction by -(27/16) hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/((X,Y) 16 pi^2) {I, int(d^*A|_V, d^*A|_V)} (nonzero, built from ([A,c],A^*)), so 'the obstruction is removed' holds only for the quadratic component.
caveats.fix: State: quadratic component removed; full one-loop QME open until the cubic special-edge triangles and quartic-vertex bubbles are computed.

caveats.text: F = (27/16) hbar tr_g(ad_X ad_Y)/((X,Y) 16 pi^2) int(d^*A|_V, d^*A|_V) is local, even, ghost number 0, dimension 4, invariant under Spin(4) x Spin(6) x Ad, translations and dilatation, and eps-independent: allowed. It is not a part of I^CT[eps], which by [C07, Thm B] lies in O_loc tensor A_{<0} and is unique; it is a finite order-hbar change of the interaction (I -> I - F), the lift of [C07, Prop 12.0.3, Lemma 12.0.4]. It is not invariant under special conformal transformations (it is the Feynman-gauge longitudinal term), so it enters the Step-2 equivariant counterterms.
caveats.fix: Write 'renormalised interaction I - I^CT[eps] - F' (as engine B does) and never 'I^CT[eps] + F'.

findings.gap: The proposition is stated 'for every g as in Def c1-spaces'. For abelian g every term of {S,S} that could distinguish the relative signs contains [-,-], so all four sign patterns and both signs of 1/2([c,c],c^*) give {S,S} = 0.
findings.fix: Restrict the third item to g with [g,g] != 0 (it is proved for su(2)).

findings.target: ch01 Prop c1-Q (pairing preservation) vs ledger X8
findings.gap: The manuscript's relation <Qe_0,e_1> + (-1)^{|e_0|}<e_0,Qe_1> = 0 is the opposite of [ESW, Def 1.16(3)] as printed, int omega(e_0,Qe_1) = (-1)^{|e_0|} int omega(Qe_0,e_1); with the manuscript's graded antisymmetry the printed ESW sign would make <A,QA> vanish for even A. The ledger resolution X8 says to use the ESW formula; the manuscript silently (and correctly) uses the other one.
findings.fix: Add one sentence recording the conflict and why the printed ESW sign is incompatible with a nonzero kinetic term.

findings.target: ch02 Prop c2-psl (super-Jacobi, Killing form, block rule)
findings.gap: 'The super-Jacobi identity holds on every unordered triple of the seven types' is supported by one random draw per type triple (superconformal/verify.py, sec_alg). For a triple with three even arguments the Schwartz-Zippel bound per draw is 1/4+1/4+1/4 = 3/4; no bound is stated for this item (Remark c2-sz covers master-equation components only). For a 30|32-dimensional algebra an exact check is cheap.
findings.fix: Verify super-Jacobi, the block rule and the Killing form exhaustively on a basis (62^3 triples) or with symbolic coefficients, or state the bound.

findings.target: ch02 Prop c2-coeff (last sentence) and Remark c2-status
findings.gap: 'With these values {S,S^(1)(x_1)} = 0 holds for all seven types' is evaluated for su(2) at sampled generators only (for Delta, special conformal and Sigma^* types no general-g argument is given). The heuristic that the identities use [-,-] only through Jacobi and (-,-) only through invariance is not a proof; su(2) satisfies additional identities (products of two structure constants reduce to products of the pairing; every invariant of four adjoints reduces to products of (-,-)), so su(2) cannot certify general g.
findings.fix: Add 'for g = su(2), at sampled generators' to the sentence; for general g repeat on a gauge algebra without these degeneracies (e.g. su(3)) or argue symbolically.

findings.gap: P(0,infty)*alpha is not compactly supported, so 'alpha is Q-exact' holds only in E_c + P(0,infty)*E_c. In E_c itself Q has cohomology.
findings.counterexample: alpha = an element of C_c^infty(R^4; g) in the c^* slot with int dvol (alpha, X) != 0 for some X in g: Q alpha = 0 (Q vanishes on the c^* slot), but the c^*-component of Q(E_c) is d^*(A^*|_V), whose integral is zero, so alpha is not Q of a compactly supported element.
findings.fix: Replace by: 'every alpha in E_c with Q alpha = 0 equals Q(P(0,infty)*alpha), with P(0,infty)*alpha smooth but not compactly supported; (E_c, Q) itself is not acyclic.'

findings.target: ch03 Cor c3-functionals, 'Hence the complex ... is acyclic'
findings.gap: The identity F = (F o h_(n)) o Q_(n) on E_c^{tensor n} is correct, but F o h_(n) is only shown to be defined on E_c^{tensor n}. Since (Q^GF)^2 != 0, P(0,infty)*P(0,infty) = int_0^infty u (Q^GF)^2 e^{-uH} du != 0, so E_c + P(0,infty)*E_c is not stable under P(0,infty)* and F o h_(n) need not extend to the domain that defines 'functionals of this type'. Acyclicity of that complex (primitive inside the complex) does not follow.
findings.fix: Either state only 'every such F is Q-exact on E_c^{tensor n} with primitive F o h_(n)', or define a decay-graded space of sections stable under Q and P(0,infty)* and prove continuity of F o h_(n) on it.

findings.target: ch03 Remark c3-story ('Q alone has trivial cohomology on functionals without constant term: every Q-closed functional at scale infinity is Q-exact')
findings.gap: The corollary's hypothesis (F defined and Q-closed on E_c + P(0,infty)*E_c) excludes exactly the nontrivial classes, and also excludes basic local functionals: int(A|_Wperp, A|_Wperp) diverges logarithmically on A|_Wperp = P(0,infty)*alpha ~ |x|^{-2}.
findings.counterexample: For fixed X in g, the linear functional e -> int dvol (c^*-component of e, X) on E_c is Q-closed (its composite with Q is int d^*(A^*|_V) = 0 on E_c) and not Q-exact (G o Q never depends on the c^*-component, because Q kills the c^* slot). On E_c + P(0,infty)*E_c it is not Q-closed (its composite with Q on P(0,infty)* c^* gives int (c^*, X) != 0), consistent with the corollary. This class is the constant gauge parameter, an infrared datum on R^4.
findings.fix: Restrict the remark to the class of Cor c3-functionals; acknowledge that zero-mode classes such as int(c^*, X) survive and are discarded by the program (ledger G1).

findings.target: ch03 Thm c3-uv, Cor c3-qme, Def c3-delta ('Delta_infty = 0, {-,-}_infty = 0')
findings.gap: On non-compact R^4 the class of functionals is not specified. For translation-invariant local functionals d_{K_eps} and d_P can diverge with the volume (Delta_eps int(A,A^*) is the volume of R^4 times a nonzero multiple of (4 pi eps)^{-2}; d_P of the product of two translation-invariant linear functionals is int int P = infinity), and 'Delta_infty = 0' holds only on functionals with integrable kernels, since int K_T(x,y) dy is the same for every T.
findings.fix: State the class (e.g. functionals with compactly supported coefficients, interactions cut off by a compactly supported density with the limit taken at the end, or identities of densities modulo total derivatives), cf. ledger G1/G4.

findings.gap: 'The obstruction to the QME and the Q-variation of observables sit on K_eps edges' omits the counterterm vertices -Q I^CT[eps] - {I, I^CT[eps]}_eps (and their delta-derivatives for observables), which carry no special edge and are indispensable (T2: +9/2 eps^{-1} from -Q I^CT[eps]).
findings.fix: '... sit on K_eps (or K_eps - K_0) edges and on the counterterm vertices -Q I^CT[eps] - {I, I^CT[eps]}_eps.'
